subject: Capacity surge request — temporary credit vs committed top-up
messages:
From: Liam Turner <liam.turner@skyware.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — potential top-up this quarter

Hi Hannah,

Quick note from our side: we expect a surge in inference volume starting mid-December tied to a customer pilot — roughly an additional ~200k tokens/month over current committed levels for the next 3–4 months. Can you outline what options we have mid-contract for covering this?

Two things we'd like to evaluate:
- A short-term credit/discount for the first 2–3 months while the pilot ramps
- Alternatively, an incremental committed top-up that we can true-up monthly rather than prepay the full remaining term upfront

Also attaching our recent usage export for your reference (usage-report-nov.csv). If you can share a simple cost comparison and how the amendment would look (DocuSign-friendly) that would be great.

Thanks,
Liam Turner
VP Engineering, Skyware
liam.turner@skyware.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Liam Turner <liam.turner@skyware.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T17:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — potential top-up this quarter

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and the export, very helpful. Two pragmatic paths we can take quickly:

Option A — Staged credit (fastest to implement)
- Apply a temporary usage credit equal to 20% of incremental usage for the first 2 months (applies only to delta above baseline)
- Credits appear on invoice as a line item; no contract amendment required if we keep it as a 60-day discretionary credit tied to usage conditions

Option B — Committed incremental top-up (more predictable unit price)
- Add a 6-month top-up commitment for the incremental tokens with a modest unit discount (roughly 10% off hosted baseline)
- Requires a short amendment to the Master Services Agreement (DocuSign) and a billing schedule; can be structured with monthly true-ups against the commit

Quick ask from our side: does Skyware prefer a light-touch credit you can turn off (Option A) or a committed top-up with lower per-token cost but a short-term commitment (Option B)? If you want, I can loop finance and CS to draft the amendment and a one-page comparison.

I've attached a draft amendment template we usually start from (amendment-draft.pdf).

Available for a 20-minute call tomorrow if you want to walk through the tradeoffs.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Attachments: usage-report-nov.csv, amendment-draft.pdf, forecast-model.xlsx

Marcus — can finance weigh in on how we prefer to structure this from a credit vs committed-revenue perspective? Also please confirm whether 20% temporary credit is feasible or if we should propose 15% for 2 months + an applied credit for month 3 instead.

Monica — can CS confirm the pilot rollout dates and whether there are any success metrics tied to the pilot that would justify the staged credit? Also need your input on whether we should require a minimal 6-month top-up if they pick the committed path.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T11:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Capacity planning — potential top-up this quarter

Hannah — good summary. From finance perspective I'd prefer a compromise option to preserve revenue while offering customer flexibility:

Recommendation (finance-approved):
- Offer a 15% temporary credit on incremental usage for the first 2 months (applies to delta above the last committed baseline).
- If incremental usage in month 3 remains >= 80% of the month-2 incremental, apply a one-time invoice credit equal to 5% of month-3 incremental usage (effectively giving them up to ~20% over three months but staged).
- Cap total credit exposure at $25k for the 3-month period.
- For the committed path, require a minimum 4-month top-up at a 10% unit discount, with monthly true-ups.

Ask legal to convert the committed path language into a short amendment if the customer picks that route. If we go the credit route, we can handle via billing ops (no amendment), but we need procurement to sign off if they need a PO.

I'll loop Legal after Hannah confirms which option Liam prefers.

Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations
marcus_lin@redwood.com
